answer: In an agent market coordinating a voyage to survey a mesa, each active identity must anchor its trading privileges with a refundable bond locked for 90 days. The protocol caps each identity at ten bids per day, so an attacker seeking 10,000 daily bids must fund 1,000 bonds. Creating names is free, but multiplying usable identities ties up capital for three months, imposing financing costs even if every bond is eventually returned.
